content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The additive shape is right and mostly idiomatic: `AssignBulkSignupWarning` mirrors `AssignNamesakeCount` (same `service(@Val Owner, OwnerRepository)` signature, `govern: [ transaction ]`, mutate-in-place), the YAML step is wired naturally into the create chain, the mapper follows the existing `membershipTier`/`locality` expression-mapping pattern, and the field/getter/setter/schema/OpenAPI additions are consistent across all four DB dialects. One structural issue:

**Duplicated, semantically-coupled "owners on this business day" count.** `AssignBulkSignupWarning.service` computes:

```java
long count = ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
    .map(Owner::getRegistrationDate)
    .filter(businessDay::equals)
    .count();
```

which is the identical stream already present in `CheckDailyOwnerLimit.service` (lines 32–35). The new class's own Javadoc makes the coupling explicit — "the same accumulation the daily-limit rule (`CheckDailyOwnerLimit`) uses, so the warning turns on at 81 while the hard cap still rejects at 100." Two functions now independently encode the same definition of "how many owners count as created on this business day." If a maintainer later changes that definition in one place (e.g. the business-day match, or filtering out soft-deleted owners), the two rules drift apart silently even though they are meant to count the same population.

Suggested fix: extract the count into a single shared helper that both steps call — e.g. a `BusinessDay.countOwnersOn(businessDay, ownerRepository)` (the `BusinessDay` helper already owns the related `rollForward` logic) or a small `OwnerRegistrations` helper. `CheckDailyOwnerLimit` compares the result against its `DAILY_LIMIT`; `AssignBulkSignupWarning` compares against `BULK_SIGNUP_THRESHOLD`. The threshold constants and the 429-vs-flag semantics stay in their respective functions; only the single definition of the count is shared, so it can't diverge.

(Note: `AssignNamesakeCount` also does its own `findAll()`, but it counts a different thing — namesakes by name — so it is not part of this duplication.)
